turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
**I recommend the high-strength carburizing/diffusion treatment regime, using the measured 1,124 MPa recipe as a data-supported starting point.** It has some evidence of a broad high-strength region, rather than relying solely on the isolated maximum of 1,190 MPa. However, these data cannot establish robustness to ±5% changes in **every** variable.

### Evidence from the supplied data

The strongest observations belong to a distinct process regime:

- NT=930, CT=930, with THT=30 and THt=THQCr=0.
- Elevated DT, with nonzero Ct and Dt.
- Low TT, typically 160–200, with Tt=120 and TCr=0.5.

This regime produces multiple results above **1,000 MPa**, substantially exceeding the conventional heat-treatment observations.

Within that regime, the highest-strength composition is:

C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0.

It was measured under two treatments, with all other variables unchanged:

| Ct | QmT | Measured fatigue strength |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 469.8 | 60 | 1,124 MPa |
| 540 | 140 | 1,190 MPa |

The first retains **94.5% of the highest measured strength**, despite the substantial combined change in Ct and QmT. This supports choosing this composition and treatment family, although it does **not** isolate either variable’s effect.

Other compositions under the same Ct=469.8, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=60 treatment achieve **1,056 and 1,082 MPa**. Thus, the recommended treatment is not supported by just one unusually high observation.

### Robustness assessment and limitation

I would choose the **observed 1,124 MPa recipe**, rather than invent an interpolated combination or assume the 1,190 MPa boundary point remains optimal under perturbation.

Nevertheless, a literal all-variable robustness guarantee is not justified:

- High-strength samples have NT and CT fixed at **930**, so their sensitivity is not identified. A +5% change also exceeds the supplied bounds.
- Tt=120 is likewise at its upper bound.
- DT=850 reduced by 5% becomes **807.5**, below the DT values observed in this high-strength treatment family.
- For zero-valued variables, a relative ±5% test produces no change; meaningful robustness testing would require an absolute tolerance.

Consequently, **1,124 MPa is an observed baseline—not a validated worst-case strength**. The proposal below is my strongest data-grounded candidate for robust optimization, but confirming “must not collapse” requires one-variable perturbation experiments, especially for NT, CT, DT, and Tt. I have not claimed fitted-model predictions or a numerical worst-case bound.

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=469.8, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=60, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0.
